title: A finite local-dimension witness in a nonempty coordinate chart
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be $S$-schemes, let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $e:T\to X$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Set $Z=Y\times_XT$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $a,b\geq0$ and suppose there is an etale $S$-morphism $h:T\to\mathbf A^{a+b}_S$ [def-sbc-affine-space] with $Z=h^{-1}(\mathbf A^a_S)$ scheme-theoretically, where $\mathbf A^a_S$ is cut out by the last $b$ coordinates $v_1,\ldots,v_b$. Assume $Z\ne\varnothing$. There exist an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, a minimal prime $s$ of $R$, and a point $t\in Z$ over $s$, such that the image of the corresponding point of $Z_s=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ in $\mathbf A^a_{\kappa(s)}$ is its generic point. Here $\kappa(s)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/s)$, a minimal prime is a prime containing no strictly smaller prime, and a generic point means a point whose closure is the whole space. For this $t$, writing $y$ for its image in $Y$ and $x=i(y)$, the local rings satisfy
$$\dim\mathcal O_{Z,t}=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}=0,\qquad \dim\mathcal O_{T,t}=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=b.$$
Dimensions are the suprema of lengths of strict prime chains [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. More explicitly, passage from these local rings over $s$ to their fibre local rings preserves their prime-poset dimensions, and the ambient affine-space fibre local ring at $h(t)$ is
$$\kappa(s)(u_1,\ldots,u_a)[v_1,\ldots,v_b]_{(v_1,\ldots,v_b)}.$$
No Noetherian, reducedness, finite-dimensionality, smoothness, or finite-type condition is imposed on $S,X,Y$ beyond the displayed etale chart hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 056G (lemma-smooth-open) for the open image of affine-space projection. Agent finite-dimensional witness argument extracted from coordinate-model Steps 8--9: minimal-base-prime choice, nil-ideal fibre reduction, etale local dimension and polynomial maximal height; the tag alone does not assert this witness.

proof.text: Let $g:Z\to\mathbf A^a_S$ be the restriction of $h$. The scheme-theoretic inverse-image hypothesis identifies $g$ with the base change of $h$ along $\mathbf A^a_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{a+b}_S$. Thus $g$ is etale. Likewise $Z\to Y$ is etale as the base change of $e$. Choose $z_0\in Z$, and an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing its image in $S$. The map $g_0:Z\times_SS_0\to\mathbf A^a_{S_0}$ is etale by base change. Its nonempty image $W$ is open. Identify $\mathbf A^a_{S_0}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R[u_1,\ldots,u_a]$ and let $P$ be the prime corresponding to $g(z_0)$.

Put $p=P\cap R$. Choose a minimal prime $s\subseteq p$ using the prime-contains-minimal-prime lemma with ideal $0$. The ideal $Q=sR[u_1,\ldots,u_a]$ is prime, since its quotient is the polynomial ring over the domain $R/s$, and $Q\subseteq P$. An open of a spectrum containing $P$ contains $Q$: choose a basic open $D(f)$ with $P\in D(f)\subseteq W$; then $f\notin P$ implies $f\notin Q$. Consequently $Q\in W$, and the definition of the image $W$ supplies a point $t\in Z\times_SS_0$ with $g_0(t)=Q$. Its image in $S_0$ is exactly $s$. Regard $t$ also as a point of $Z$.

source.place: Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), existence of a minimal prime below a prime; elementary polynomial and basic-open calculation

proof.text: Write $k_s=\kappa(s)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/s)$. This identification follows by reducing fractions in $R_s/sR_s$: the images of $R\setminus s$ are exactly the nonzero elements of $R/s$. In the fibre $Z_s$, the chosen point maps to the zero prime of $k_s[u_1,\ldots,u_a]$, because $Q=sR[u]$ becomes the zero ideal after first inverting $R\setminus s$ and then reducing modulo $s$. The zero prime is the generic point: it lies below every prime, so its closure is the whole spectrum. Put $K=k_s(u_1,\ldots,u_a)$, with $K=k_s$ if $a=0$. The affine-stalk localization lemma gives $\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^a_{k_s},g_s(t)}=k_s[u]_{(0)}=K$.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6); elementary localization calculations in polynomial rings

proof.text: In $\mathbf A^{a+b}_{k_s}$ the image $h_s(t)$ is the prime $(v_1,\ldots,v_b)$ of $k_s[u,v]$: its contraction to $k_s[u]$ is zero and its quotient on the coordinate subspace is the zero prime. Hence its affine local ring is $k_s[u,v]_{(v)}$. There is a canonical isomorphism $k_s[u,v]_{(v)}\cong K[v]_{(v)}$. Indeed every nonzero polynomial in $u$ is already inverted on the left. The remaining denominators are exactly polynomials with nonzero constant coefficient in $v$, on both sides. Clearing the finitely many $u$-denominators in a fraction over $K[v]$ gives the inverse map. Thus the ambient fibre local ring has exactly the displayed form in the statement.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6); elementary localization calculations in polynomial rings

proof.text: The field $K$ has dimension zero, since its only prime ideal is $(0)$. Apply the polynomial-origin local-ring lemma over $K$ with $d=b$. It states that $K[v_1,\ldots,v_b]_{(v_1,\ldots,v_b)}$ has dimension $b$. Combined with the preceding identifications, the target local rings of $g_s$ and $h_s$ have dimensions $0$ and $b$, respectively. This also covers $b=0$, when the second local ring is $K$.

source.place: Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space), applied over the field kappa(s)(u_1,...,u_a)

proof.text: The fibre morphisms $g_s:Z_s\to\mathbf A^a_{k_s}$ and $h_s:T_s\to\mathbf A^{a+b}_{k_s}$ are etale by base change. Apply etale local dimension invariance to each at the chosen point. To apply the ring version, take affine target neighborhoods of the image and affine source neighborhoods inside their inverse images; the induced maps on coordinate rings are etale by the affine-local characterization of an etale morphism, and their prime localizations are the scheme stalks. Thus $\dim\mathcal O_{Z_s,t}=0$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{T_s,t}=b$, with no Noetherian assumption.

By the minimal-prime localization lemma, every element of the maximal ideal $m_s=sR_s$ of $R_s$ is nilpotent. For any one of $V=Z,T,Y,X$ and its chosen point $v=t,t,y,x$ over $s$, its image in $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ is nilpotent as well. The extended ideal $J=m_s\mathcal O_{V,v}$ consists of nilpotent elements: if $z=\sum_{j=1}^n c_j r_j$ with $r_j^{N_j}=0$, then $z^{1+\sum_j(N_j-1)}=0$, since every monomial in the expansion contains some $r_j^{N_j}$. This proves nilness of $J$, without asserting any uniform nilpotence exponent for $J$ itself.

source.place: Tag 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring); elementary binomial argument for finite sums of nilpotent elements

proof.text: The fibre-stalk quotient lemma identifies $\mathcal O_{V_s,v}$ with $\mathcal O_{V,v}/J$ for each of these four $V$. Every prime ideal contains $J$, since a prime containing a power contains the element itself. Thus contraction along the quotient map is an inclusion-preserving bijection from primes of $\mathcal O_{V,v}/J$ to all primes of $\mathcal O_{V,v}$, with inverse $P\mapsto P/J$. These inverse maps preserve strict inclusions, hence preserve every finite strict prime chain and its length. Their dimension suprema are equal, even when infinite. In particular $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,t}=0$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}=b$, and the asserted dimension preservation also holds for $Y$ and $X$.

source.place: Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre), first isomorphism; elementary prime-ideal correspondence for a quotient by a nil ideal

proof.text: Finally apply etale local dimension invariance to $Z\to Y$ and $e:T\to X$ at $t$, with images $y$ and $x$. As in Step 6, affine charts and the affine-stalk localization lemma reduce each application to the ring statement. This gives $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,t}=0$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}=b$. The fibre-product relation defining $Z$ gives $x=i(y)$. Together with Steps 2--4 and 8 this supplies the chosen affine base, minimal prime, generic fibre image, explicit ambient fibre local ring, and all dimension assertions.

proof_origin.place: Witness argument assembled from Tags 00E0, 00EU, 00OP; morphisms.tex Tags 02GO and 03WT; more-algebra.tex Tag 07QP; schemes.tex Tags 01HV and 0HA1. Realizes the finite-dimension portion extracted from the coordinate-model argument.
